Hi Elena, Monica —

Thanks for the questions. I ran through Arcadia’s questionnaire and pasted concise answers below; I also attached an export of our current subprocessor register (subprocessors_2026-11.csv).

Q1 (KMS/BYOK):
- Default: Redwood manages encryption keys in a cloud KMS (AWS KMS or GCP KMS) depending on customer region. Keys are rotated per policy (90–365 day cadence depending on data type).
- BYOK: Supported for Dedicated and Private deployments via KMS integrations; for hosted customers we offer a managed KMS option and a customer-managed key for enterprise plans (we can enable per-contract).

Q2 (Embeddings/raw text persistence):
- High-level: transient request tokens and KV cache used for attention are ephemeral and not persisted beyond session TTL (configurable, typically minutes).
- Persisted artifacts: embeddings and model outputs are optionally persisted — by default we do not persist full raw request bodies for hosted plans unless customer opts in for debugging. When persisted, data is encrypted at rest and access-controlled.

Q3 (Logs & retention):
- Application logs: default retention 30 days (configurable). Access logs (request metadata) retained 90 days. Backups are encrypted and replicated per region; we can provide documentation of where replicas live on a per-customer basis.

Additional notes:
- We are SOC 2 Type II and can share report dates.
- Subprocessor CSV includes country and function columns; if Arcadia needs a third-party assessment for a critical vendor we can coordinate a vendor questionnaire.

Attachment: subprocessors_2026-11.csv (csv)

Let us know which specific data fields Arcadia considers regulated PII (PHI subset) and we’ll provide a field-level mapping for the dataflow diagram.

Best,

Hi Elena —

Following up on the technical asks:

1) BYOK and region-bound KMS for hosted:
- Short answer: for standard hosted plans we do not provision customer-controlled keys per-tenant automatically; however for enterprise contracts we offer a \"hosted-with-customer-KMS\" option where the customer supplies a key (BYOK) tied to region-specific KMS. This can be enabled in the onboarding flow and enforced with routing rules so that backups and replicas for EU-scoped customers remain in EU KMS.

2) Redaction/hash at ingestion:
- We provide a pre-processing hook (pre-ingest pipeline) where Arcadia can supply a regex/field-list to redact, hash, or tokenize before any embedding or storage occurs. This is commonly used by healthcare customers to strip PHI.

3) Embeddings and search indices:
- If Arcadia opts to persist embeddings, we store embeddings encrypted and with strict RBAC; we can also offer a policy that prevents creating persistent indexes for specific datasets (no persistence).

4) Evidence bundle & DPA redlines:
- We can accept redlines for Section 5; Monica and I will coordinate legal/tech responses. I uploaded an updated sanitized dataflow to a shared Drive (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-arcadia-dataflow) that reflects field-level boundaries and where PHI is redacted in transit.

If Arcadia can send the DPA redline and a short list of fields you consider PHI (e.g., patient_id, mrn, full_name, dob, address), we’ll produce a field-level mapping and an updated diagram within 48 hours.

Thanks,
